t: The oldest of the South Arabian kingdoms, centred on the irrigated oasis of Marib in Yemen, and the biblical land of Sheba.
It grew rich on irrigated farming and on frankincense and myrrh carried by caravan to the Mediterranean and Mesopotamia.
Rivals, sea trade and the rise of Himyar wore it down until Himyar absorbed it around 275 CE.
dyk: Besides formal inscriptions on stone, the Sabaeans wrote letters and contracts in a cursive script on palm-leaf stalks, and many of these everyday texts have been recovered.
ev: Mukarribs rule Saba from Marib and Sirwah; Sabaic inscriptions appear
Itamra the Sabaean sends gifts to Sargon II of Assyria
Karib’il Watar destroys Awsan and imposes Sabaean supremacy in South Arabia
The Himyarite kingdom rises in the highlands around Zafar
Aelius Gallus besieges Marib for six days and retreats
Sha’irum Awtar defeats Hadramawt and takes Shabwa
Shammar Yuhar’ish of Himyar absorbs Saba

f.capital: Marib (with Sirwah as an early centre)
